rounds.text: Pelatro Ltd is significantly under-appreciated by the market, trading at a modest P/E ratio of 17.3x [E1] while delivering explosive top and bottom-line expansion with 47% compounded sales growth and 58% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E14, E15]. This exceptional growth is paired with high profitability, demonstrated by a stellar 19.3% ROE and an 11.27% ROA that comfortably dwarf sector benchmarks of 4.29% and 2% respectively [E8, E9]. Furthermore, operational efficiency is on a steep upward trajectory, with operating margins expanding by 14 percentage points over three years to reach 20% in the TTM and pushing even higher to 22% in the most recent quarter [E19, E20]. Cash generation remains robust and reliable, backed by a strong cash conversion ratio of 1.11x and Rs 20 Cr in operating cash flow for March 2026 [E23, E24]. Valuation models reflect a clear mispricing, as a discounted cash flow analysis estimates intrinsic value at Rs 472 per share—offering a tangible margin of safety—while the reverse DCF indicates that the current market price of Rs 390 only prices in a modest 7.3% earnings growth expectation [E2, E34, E36]. Conceded: free cash flow stood at Rs -20 Cr in March 2026 [E25].

Despite reported profit growth, Pelatro Ltd carries severe underlying cash generation and working capital risks that undermine the quality of its earnings [E25, E42]. Specifically, free cash flow collapsed to negative Rs 20 Cr in March 2026 despite strong operating cash flow of Rs 20 Cr, signalling heavy capital drains [E24, E25]. Furthermore, working capital days have dramatically deteriorated, surging from 35.9 days up to 96.8 days [E42]. Valuation multiples also reflect a premium over sector benchmarks, with the P/E ratio at 18.35x versus a sector benchmark of 15.66x and EV/EBITDA at 12.33x against an 8.89x sector benchmark [E6, E11]. Institutional confidence is visibly retreating, evidenced by foreign institutions cutting their stake from 5.56% to 2.41% and domestic institutions reducing theirs from 3.61% to 1.57% since September 2024, alongside a minor promoter stake reduction [E30, E31, E32]. Additionally, filed statements explicitly flag that the current tax rate seems low, introducing potential future earnings volatility [E41]. Conceded: [E14, E15, E19].

While the bear highlights a negative free cash flow of Rs -20 Cr in March 2026, operating cash flow stood robust at Rs 20 Cr, and cash conversion was a healthy 1.11x, confirming that profits are fully backed by cash [E23, E24, E25]. The concern over valuation premiums ignores that the company’s return metrics massively outpace sector medians, with an ROA of 11.27% versus a sector benchmark of 2% and an ROE of 19.3% against 4.29% [E6, E8, E9, E11]. Conceded: [E42]. On institutional ownership, while holdings shifted, the business itself is starting to outperform expectations, with profit growth exceeding 1-year price growth by 52% and results scoring a perfect 100/100 on fundamental improvement [E31, E32, E38, E49]. Furthermore, borrowings actually decreased from Rs 41 Cr to Rs 39 Cr by September 2026, accompanied by a comfortable current ratio of 3.22x, demonstrating sound financial management despite working capital shifts [E27, E28, E42]. Conceded: [E41].

Conceded: [E23], [E24]. Despite robust operating cash flow, the bull's dismissal of the negative free cash flow ignores a staggering absolute cash drain of Rs -20 Cr in March 2026 [E25]. The bull relies heavily on superior return metrics like ROA and ROE, yet fails to address that these multiples come with a valuation premium, trading at a P/E of 18.35x against a sector benchmark of 15.66x and an EV/EBITDA of 12.33x versus a sector benchmark of 8.89x [E6, E11]. On the matter of institutional confidence, the bull highlights performance outperformance [E38], but glosses over the continuous exodus of institutional capital, with foreign institutions slashing holdings from 5.56% to 2.41% and domestic institutions dropping from 3.61% to 1.57% since September 2024 [E31, E32]. Furthermore, promoter stake has also trended downward from 53.59% to 52.62% over the same period [E30]. Conceded: [E28], [E27]. Finally, the bull glosses over the operational red flags explicitly flagged in the filings, including a low tax rate and a severe ballooning of working capital days from 35.9 days to 96.8 days [E41, E42].
